about: AI scripts: how to run a whole job with an AI in one or two rounds. Source: v2/briefs/scripts/scripts.js (node build.js). Edit the source, never this file.
method: Give context once. Put your business brain in the project or custom instructions so you never paste it again.
Attach files instead of pasting them, and say what each file is for.
One complete ask beats five small ones: say what done looks like, what to avoid, and how to check it.
On big jobs, ask for a short plan first and approve it. A plan costs a few lines; a wrong build costs the whole build.
Make it check its own work before it shows you (screenshots, a checklist, a reread against your ask).
Collect every change, then send them in one message. Say what to keep.
Ask for only what changed, not the whole thing again.
When a chat gets long or starts repeating mistakes, get a handoff summary and start a fresh chat with it.
When a prompt works, save it as a skill or a saved prompt so next time is one line.

scripts.title: Any AI job in one round
scripts.when: Before any job you would normally go back and forth on. The method under every other script.
scripts.outcome: A finished piece in one build and at most one round of changes, without re-explaining your business.

variables.label: The job
variables.example: A one-page welcome guide for new cleaning clients

variables.label: What done looks like
variables.example: One page, friendly, covers what to expect on day one, ready to send as a PDF

variables.label: What to avoid
variables.example: No corporate words, no prices, nothing longer than one page

steps.title: The full ask
steps.why: Everything the AI needs, in one message, including how it will be judged.

steps.title: Check before showing
steps.why: Most second rounds are things the AI could have caught itself.
steps.say: Before you show me, check your work against my ask line by line. Mark each point pass or fail, fix every fail, then show me the result and the checklist. No recap of my ask.

steps.title: One round of changes
steps.why: Ten small corrections cost ten rounds. One list costs one.
steps.say:
Here are all my changes in one go. Keep everything else exactly as it is.
KEEP: [what you like]
CHANGE:
1. [where]: [what is wrong] -> [what you want]
2. ...
Send back only the parts that changed, one line per change.

steps.title: Save it
steps.why: The next time is one line instead of a page.

savers: Give context once. Put your business brain in the project or custom instructions so you never paste it again.
Attach files instead of pasting them, and say what each file is for.
One complete ask beats five small ones: say what done looks like, what to avoid, and how to check it.
On big jobs, ask for a short plan first and approve it. A plan costs a few lines; a wrong build costs the whole build.
Make it check its own work before it shows you (screenshots, a checklist, a reread against your ask).
Collect every change, then send them in one message. Say what to keep.
Ask for only what changed, not the whole thing again.
When a chat gets long or starts repeating mistakes, get a handoff summary and start a fresh chat with it.
When a prompt works, save it as a skill or a saved prompt so next time is one line.

scripts.title: A premium website, built right the first time
scripts.when: You want a site or landing page with real motion and a premium feel, built by an AI that writes code (Claude or similar).
scripts.outcome: A working one-page site that passes its own checklist on phone and desktop, after one build and one round of changes.

variables.label: Business
variables.example: Northside Detailing, mobile car detailing in Austin

variables.label: 2 or 3 references you love
variables.example: apple.com/airpods-pro, aesop.com, the opening of Blade Runner 2049

variables.label: The one thing a visitor should do
variables.example: Book a detail

steps.title: Write the brief
steps.why: The look, the intro, the scroll moment and the never-list, decided before any code. Most rounds come from these being guessed.

steps.title: Learn from your references
steps.why: Gives the AI designer words for what you like, so it stops guessing "modern".

steps.title: Plan before code
steps.why: Fixing a plan takes one line. Fixing a build takes a rebuild.
steps.say: Here is my brief (attached) for {{business}}. Before writing any code, give me: the sections in order, the one intro move, the one scroll moment, the fonts and colors, and what phones get instead of the heavy parts. Ten lines at most. Wait for my OK.

steps.title: Build and check yourself
steps.why: The AI screenshots its own page and fixes it before you see it.
steps.say: Approved. Build it. Before you show me: take screenshots at 390px and 1440px (top, middle, end) and frames at 0s, 0.5s, 1s and 2s of the intro. Check them against the brief's checklist and against my references ({{references}}). Fix every fail, check once more, then send the files, the screenshots and the marked checklist.

steps.title: One round of changes
steps.why: Gut-feel words like "feels cheap" become exact instructions.

steps.title: Before it goes live
steps.why: Catches the things that cost trust: a vague headline, a claim you can't back.
steps.add: The page must make "{{action}}" obvious in the first screen on a phone.

savers: Attach your logo, photos and brand colors in the first message, not when it asks.
Name the stack in the brief (for example HTML + GSAP, or Three.js for real 3D) so it doesn't pick something heavy.
Ask for changed files only after the first build.
If you've gone three rounds on one detail, stop and use the change step: say the gut feel and what to keep.

scripts.title: A hero that comes alive
scripts.when: One signature moment: a logo that forms, a product reveal, a hero that moves like it's alive instead of sitting still.
scripts.outcome: A live hero with a real intro, motion at rest, one scroll moment, and a still poster for phones and speed.

variables.label: The star
variables.example: Our logo

variables.label: It starts as
variables.example: Loose water under a dark surface

variables.label: It ends as
variables.example: The logo, fully formed in clear glass, floating

steps.title: Write the brief
steps.why: Start state, end state, how it forms, how it stays alive, and the never-list (no staged glow, no floor line, no fade-in).

steps.title: Storyboard first
steps.why: Four frames in words are cheap to fix. Rendered motion is not.
steps.say: From my brief (attached), describe the intro as four frames: 0s, 0.5s, 1s and the final frame. Then say what moves after the intro and what happens on scroll. Words only, no code yet. Wait for my OK.

steps.title: Build it live
steps.why: Real-time beats a moving picture. This was the round that made the 127 hero feel alive.
steps.say: Approved. Build {{subject}} live in the browser (real-time, not a video or a picture being moved). It starts as: {{start}}. It ends as: {{end}}. It must visibly form, not fade or slide in. Paint a still poster of the final frame first, start the live version after the page loads, pause it offscreen, and give phones without a real graphics chip the poster.

steps.title: Prove it's alive
steps.why: Static is the most common miss. Frames make it obvious.
steps.say: Grab frames at 0s, 0.5s, 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s, and one mid-scroll. Check: the middle frames show it forming; frames after the intro differ (it keeps moving); nothing on my never-list shows; the poster matches the final frame. Fix and send the frames with the checklist.

steps.title: One round of changes
steps.why: Send "too static" or "feels staged" as chips plus what to keep, all at once.

savers: Say "centered, facing forward" and the material (glass, liquid, metal) up front. Those were three rounds on the 127 hero.
Ask for frames, not a description. You can judge frames in seconds.
Keep the poster rule in every ask, or speed scores drop.

scripts.title: A short ad or reel
scripts.when: A 15 to 30 second ad or reel that comes out on brand, with words that hold up.
scripts.outcome: A script, shot prompts for your AI video tool, an edit plan and a claims check, in one sitting.

variables.label: What you're showing
variables.example: Our interior detail

variables.label: Who it's for
variables.example: Parents with a messy SUV

variables.label: The first 2 seconds
variables.example: A crumb-covered back seat, then one swipe and it's clean

steps.title: Write the brief
steps.why: Hook, exact words, format, look and the never-list in one place.

steps.title: Script
steps.why: Words first. Visuals follow the words.

steps.title: Shot prompts
steps.why: One prompt per shot, written for your video tool, so you aren't rerolling.

steps.title: Edit plan
steps.why: Cut order, captions and timing before you open the editor.

steps.title: Claims check
steps.why: Nothing promised that you can't back.

savers: Generate 2 or 3 versions of the first shot only, pick one, then do the rest. The hook is where rerolls pay off.
Keep the exact on-screen words in the brief so every tool gets the same words.

scripts.title: From offer to sales page
scripts.when: You know what you sell and need the offer and the page that explains it, without five drafts.
scripts.outcome: A clear offer, a sales page draft, and a page a stranger gets in five seconds.

variables.label: What you do
variables.example: Weekly lawn care

variables.label: Who buys it
variables.example: Homeowners who travel for work

steps.title: Shape the offer
steps.why: A page can't fix a fuzzy offer.

steps.title: Answer the no's first
steps.why: The page has to answer them, so write them down now.

steps.title: Write the page
steps.why: Feed it the offer and the objections from the last two steps.
steps.add: Use the offer and the objections above. Answer each objection somewhere on the page.

steps.title: Five-second test
steps.why: If a stranger doesn't get it fast, nothing else matters.

steps.title: Claims check
steps.why: Real proof only.

savers: Do all five steps in one chat so each step can use the last one's answer.
Paste real customer words if you have them. They beat anything the AI writes.

scripts.title: Your first outreach batch
scripts.when: You're ready to contact real people and want a list, first messages and follow-ups drafted for you to send.
scripts.outcome: A list with a reason to contact each person, first messages and follow-ups drafted for you to read and send yourself.

variables.label: What you offer
variables.example: Same-week bookkeeping cleanup

variables.label: Who it's for
variables.example: Restaurant owners in Phoenix

steps.title: Build the list
steps.why: A reason per person is what makes a message worth reading.

steps.title: First messages
steps.why: One message per person, built on the reason you found.

steps.title: Follow-ups
steps.why: Drafted now so you aren't writing them cold later.

steps.title: When they reply
steps.why: Paste the thread and get the best next message.

savers: Ask for a table (name, reason, message) so you can scan and edit in one pass.
You send every message yourself. Emails carry your address and a way to opt out.

scripts.title: A week of content in one sitting
scripts.when: You keep staring at a blank screen. Plan, hook and script a week in one chat.
scripts.outcome: Hooks, a week of posts and scripts for the videos, all in your voice.

variables.label: Business
variables.example: A home bakery doing custom cakes

variables.label: Who you're talking to
variables.example: Parents planning kids' birthdays

steps.title: Hooks
steps.why: The first line decides if anyone watches the rest.

steps.title: The week
steps.why: Pick from the hooks; plan seven posts.
steps.add: Plan 7 days only, using the best hooks above.

steps.title: Scripts
steps.why: Script the video posts in one go.
steps.add: Write a script for each video post in the plan above.

steps.title: One into ten
steps.why: Your best post becomes the next week.

savers: Save your voice guide in your project instructions once, so every post sounds like you without asking.
Ask for everything in one table you can copy into your scheduler.

scripts.title: Research a market in one pass
scripts.when: You need to know a market and the people winning in it before you spend time or money.
scripts.outcome: A short market brief and a teardown of five players, with sources and how sure the AI is.

variables.label: Market
variables.example: Mobile pet grooming in Denver

variables.label: The decision this research is for
variables.example: Should I charge per visit or monthly?

steps.title: Market brief
steps.why: Numbers and trends first.

steps.title: Five-player teardown
steps.why: How the winners find buyers, price and deliver.

steps.title: Decide
steps.why: Research only pays off as a decision.
steps.say: Using the brief and teardown above, answer one question: {{question}}. Give your answer, the three facts it rests on with sources, how sure you are, and what would change your mind. Under 150 words.

savers: Start with the decision you need to make. It stops the AI from writing a report nobody acts on.
Ask for sources and a confidence level on every number. Treat anything unsourced as a guess.

scripts.title: Read your numbers and pick the move
scripts.when: Once a week. Paste the numbers, get the one move, not a lecture.
scripts.outcome: The one move for the week, and the math behind it.

variables.label: Goal right now
variables.example: 10 booked jobs a week

steps.title: Read the week
steps.why: One move, with the math shown.

steps.title: Check the money
steps.why: When spend is the question, check runway before deciding.

savers: Paste the same table every week (same columns, same order) so the AI compares like with like.
Keep a numbers doc in your Brain and point the AI at it instead of pasting history.

scripts.title: Turn repeat work into a one-line ask
scripts.when: You've given your AI the same instructions three times. Do it once properly.
scripts.outcome: A written SOP and a saved skill or project, so next time you type one line.

variables.label: The repeat job
variables.example: Writing the Friday project update email

steps.title: Write the SOP
steps.why: The steps, written once.

steps.title: Package it
steps.why: Your best example plus the SOP becomes a reusable skill.
steps.add: Use the SOP above as the instructions.

savers: Include one example you were happy with. One good example beats a page of rules.

scripts.title: Start fresh without losing anything
scripts.when: The chat is long, slow, repeating mistakes, or forgetting what you said. Long chats cost more on every message.
scripts.outcome: A short handoff you paste into a new chat, so it picks up exactly where you were.

steps.title: Get the handoff
steps.why: Everything that matters, in a page instead of a hundred messages.
steps.say: We're moving to a new chat. Write a handoff under 300 words: the goal, decisions made (and why), what's done, what's left in order, files and links in use, and the mistakes not to repeat. Plain list, no recap of our conversation.

steps.title: Start the new chat
steps.why: A clean start with the handoff costs less on every message from here.
steps.say:
Here's the handoff from my last chat. Read it, tell me in two lines what you'll do next, then do it.

[paste the handoff]

savers: If your AI has projects, put the handoff in the project files so every new chat starts with it.
